Jurisdictions.meta_description: Find which rule decides whether electronic evidence is accepted, anywhere in the world.
Jurisdictions.page_title: In what jurisdiction will you be using this?
Jurisdictions.page_description: Type the country, state or province of the court. We tell you the rule that decides whether electronic evidence is accepted there, and what Celia does to meet it.
Jurisdictions.search_placeholder: Try New York or United Kingdom
Jurisdictions.status_built: Celia is built to this rule.
Jurisdictions.status_mapped: Mapped. Counsel has not confirmed it yet.
Jurisdictions.none_message: We haven’t mapped {name} yet. Tell us which court and we will add it.
Jurisdictions.kind_certificate_text: The person responsible for the system certifies how the record was made.
Jurisdictions.kind_certificate_answer: Our certificate names the system, the time and the method.
Jurisdictions.kind_authentication_text: You show the record is what it claims to be and that the system kept it intact.
Jurisdictions.kind_authentication_answer: The report is hashed against the commitment, so any change shows.
Jurisdictions.kind_presumption_text: The system is presumed to have worked unless someone challenges it.
Jurisdictions.kind_presumption_answer: The method was fixed before any data was touched.
Jurisdictions.kind_equal_text: A record can’t be refused only because it is electronic.
Jurisdictions.kind_equal_answer: Every finding states what is proven and what is not.
Jurisdictions.disclaimer: These are research notes, not legal advice. Rules named by section come from public sources; the rest are national electronic transactions laws based on the UN Model Law on Electronic Commerce (UNCITRAL). We confirm each with counsel before we say it is met.

Staff.report_error_words: The text declares fraud or promises an outcome. Say what is proven and not proven.

Staff.evidence_error_words: The report refuses that wording. Describe what it shows without declaring fraud.

Staff.evidence_error_full: A case holds at most {max} pieces of evidence.

App.meta_description: Report crypto fraud, get professional access, and follow a case from evidence to court. Celia holds no funds and does not declare fraud.

Email.claim_submitted_body: We have your claim. Sign in to see where it stands.
Email.ownership_confirmed_body: We checked the proof you gave us. It shows you control the wallet. It does not mean your claim is accepted. Sign in to see your claim.
Email.claim_validated_body: A person at Celia checked your claim and the evidence you added. It does not mean a lawyer has taken your case. Sign in to see your claim.
Email.claim_in_review_preview: A person is looking at your claim.

Email.claim_rejected_subject: We could not accept your claim
Email.claim_rejected_preview: We could not accept your claim.
Email.claim_rejected_heading: We could not accept your claim
Email.claim_rejected_body: We reviewed your claim and could not accept it. Sign in to read why.
Email.claim_in_case_subject: Your claim is now part of a case
Email.claim_in_case_preview: Your claim now sits in a case.
Email.claim_in_case_heading: Your claim is now part of a case
Email.claim_in_case_body: Your claim now sits in a case with other claims about the same platform. Sign in to read its summary.
Email.case_sealed_subject: We have enough evidence for your case
Email.case_sealed_heading: We have enough evidence for your case
Email.case_sealed_body: We have enough evidence on your case. This decides nothing: a court decides. A firm can now choose to take the case, but none has to. Sign in to read the summary.
Email.case_taken_subject: A lawyer or firm has taken the case your claim is part of
Email.case_taken_preview: A lawyer or firm has taken the case.
Email.case_taken_heading: A lawyer or firm has taken the case your claim is part of
Email.case_taken_body: A lawyer or firm has taken the case your claim is part of. They run it, not Celia. Celia does not hold funds or pay anyone.
Email.counsel_received_body: We are checking your application against public records. You can browse the case bank now. Your account opens once we have approved it.
Email.counsel_verified_body: We approved your application. You can now take cases. Whether you may act in a case is still for you to confirm.
Email.counsel_review_reset_subject: Your registration is under review again
Email.counsel_review_reset_preview: We are checking your registration again.
Email.counsel_review_reset_heading: Your registration is under review again
Email.counsel_review_reset_body: You changed the jurisdictions you listed, so we are checking them again. You cannot take a new case until we have finished.
Email.application_rejected_subject: We could not approve your application
Email.application_rejected_preview: We could not approve your application.
Email.application_rejected_heading: We could not approve your application
Email.application_rejected_body: We checked your application and could not approve it. Sign in to read the reason and to see when you can apply again.
Email.case_ready_for_counsel_preview: A case is open to firms.
Email.case_ready_for_counsel_body: A case with enough evidence is open to firms. Sign in to read the summary.
Email.case_taken_by_you_body: You now hold this case on Celia, and other firms can no longer take it. You run it, not Celia.
Email.contact_request_subject: An organisation asks to contact you
Email.contact_request_preview: Nothing is shared unless you say yes.
Email.contact_request_heading: An organisation asks to contact you
Email.contact_request_body: A verified organisation working on a case you joined has asked to contact you. Nothing is shared with it unless you say yes. Sign in to read its request and answer.
Email.contact_request_decided_subject: Your request to contact claimants was answered
Email.contact_request_decided_preview: Sign in to see the answer.
Email.contact_request_decided_body: Celia has answered your request to contact claimants. Sign in to see the answer and who has agreed.
Email.footer_account: You get this email because you have a Celia account. It is an account notice, so it is always sent.
Email.footer_updates: You get this email because you have a Celia account.

Report.notebook_none: No notebook was linked in this version. A newer version may have one.
Report.disclaimer: This report states what the chain shows and what it does not. It declares no fraud: a court decides intent.
Report.verify_text: The report hash identifies exactly these findings: change a word and it no longer matches. The method commitment is the hash of the plan that was approved before the analysis ran.

ReportedPattern.title: What may have happened
ReportedPattern.note: Their own accounts, not a finding of fraud: a court decides.
ReportedPattern.investment_platform: put money into an investment platform and could not withdraw
ReportedPattern.rug_pull: bought a token or NFT and the team disappeared
ReportedPattern.exchange_service: lost access to funds held by an exchange or wallet service
ReportedPattern.impersonation: sent crypto to someone who presented themselves as someone else
ReportedPattern.recovery_scam: paid a fund-recovery service and got nothing back
ReportedPattern.address_poisoning: sent money to a lookalike of an address they use
ReportedPattern.honeypot_token: bought a token they could not sell
ReportedPattern.extortion: were threatened and asked for crypto
ReportedPattern.fake_job: deposited crypto for work that never paid
ReportedPattern.account_takeover: had someone take over their account
ReportedPattern.romance_scam: were asked for money by someone they had met online
ReportedPattern.phishing: lost money after using a fake website, link or message
ReportedPattern.hack_exploit: lost money when a service, app or contract they used was hacked
ReportedPattern.other: lost money in a way that fits none of the listed kinds

ClaimPage.meta_description_new: Add your wallet and the platform, then tell us what happened.
ClaimPage.meta_description_detail: Follow your claim and finish the steps.
ClaimPage.address_hint_edit: A different wallet clears your ownership proof, so you will sign again for it.
ClaimPage.destination_hint: The address the money went to, if you have it. Add more below if it went to several. It lets us follow the money.
ClaimPage.error_date: Use a real date that is not in the future, with the last payment after the first.
ClaimPage.q_payment_more: The money and where it went (optional)
ClaimPage.more_text: Each wallet and transaction is a piece of evidence. Add every one you know of, on any chain. Skip what you do not have.
ClaimPage.more_affected_title: Other wallets of yours that were affected
ClaimPage.more_affected_hint: Any other wallet of yours that lost money, on any chain.
ClaimPage.more_transactions_hint: Every other transaction that moved your money, with its chain and hash.
ClaimPage.more_receiving_hint: Every address the money went to, on any chain. Each one can be traced.
ClaimPage.error_more: Check this list. Each entry must fit its chain and appear only once.
ClaimPage.edit_sent_notice: Your claim has been sent. If you change its details, a person at Celia reviews it again. A different wallet needs a new proof that it is yours. What you had before is kept on record.
ClaimPage.meta_description_edit: Change what you entered before you send your claim.
ClaimPage.delete_text: The draft and everything you entered are removed. This can’t be undone.
ClaimPage.delete_failed: This draft could not be deleted.

ClaimPage.platform_placeholder: The name of the app or site

ClaimPage.submit_others: {count, plural, one {1 other person has reported {platform}. Sending connects your claim to theirs.} other {# other people have reported {platform}. Sending connects your claim to theirs.}}
ClaimPage.submit_others_unnamed: {count, plural, one {1 other person has reported something that matches. Sending connects your claim to theirs.} other {# other people have reported something that matches. Sending connects your claim to theirs.}}
ClaimPage.sent_text: Our agent will review and confirm your claim and the evidence you added. If others report the same platform, your claim will be pooled with theirs. We will tell you here when that happens.
ClaimPage.sent_late_text: Our agent will review your claim and the evidence you added. We already had enough evidence on this platform before you sent it, so your claim is not in that file. We will tell you here what happens next.
ClaimPage.error_statement_first: Add your account of what happened first.
ClaimPage.q_what_note: Tick every one that fits. Celia works best when many people were affected by the same operator. We can’t promise that a lawyer takes any case.
ClaimPage.type_investment_platform_text: Promised returns, then no withdrawals or new fees.
ClaimPage.type_rug_pull_text: I bought a token or NFT and the team went quiet.
ClaimPage.type_exchange_service_text: It froze my funds, shut down or lost my balance.
ClaimPage.type_impersonation_text: Someone posed as support or a partner for crypto.
ClaimPage.type_recovery_scam_text: I paid a fee to get my money back. Nothing came.
ClaimPage.type_wallet_drained_text: My wallet was emptied by a link, app or stolen keys.
ClaimPage.type_address_poisoning_text: I paid a lookalike address planted in my history.
ClaimPage.type_honeypot_token_text: I bought a token that would not let me sell.
ClaimPage.type_extortion_text: Someone threatened me and demanded crypto.
ClaimPage.type_fake_job_text: I deposited crypto for work that never paid.
ClaimPage.type_account_takeover_text: Someone got into my exchange or wallet account.
ClaimPage.type_other_text: None of these fit. Tell us in your own words.
ClaimPage.pay_offchain_note: A bank or card payment does not show on a chain, so there is no wallet or transaction to add. Tell us what happened on the next steps.
ClaimPage.type_romance_scam_text: Someone I got close to online asked me for money or crypto.
ClaimPage.type_phishing_text: I used a fake site, link or message and lost money.
ClaimPage.type_hack_exploit_text: A service, app or contract I used was hacked.
ClaimPage.hint_romance_scam: Where did you meet, how long were you in touch, and what did they ask you to pay for? How much did you send, and when?

ClaimPage.hint_hack_exploit: Which service, app or contract was hacked, and when? How did you find out, and what did you lose?
ClaimPage.fraud_description_label: What kind of fraud was it? (optional)
ClaimPage.fraud_description_placeholder: Describe it in your own words

ClaimPage.connect_label: I agree that my claim is connected to the claims of other people who reported the same platform.

ClaimPage.error_truthful: Confirm this to send your claim.

ClaimPage.wallet_mobile_app: Mobile app (such as Trust Wallet or Coinbase Wallet)
ClaimPage.wallet_hardware: Hardware wallet (such as Ledger or Trezor)
ClaimPage.chain_payment_label: Which chain was the payment on?
ClaimPage.tx_hint: The ID of the payment that sent the money. Your exchange, the ATM receipt or your wallet history shows it. It lets us find where the money went.
ClaimPage.error_tx: This transaction hash does not look right for this chain.
ClaimPage.q_who: Who do you think was behind it?
ClaimPage.unknown_operator: I don’t know who it was
ClaimPage.operator_name: Name of the platform, project or person
ClaimPage.contact_social_dating: A dating app or social media
ClaimPage.contact_messaging: A Telegram or WhatsApp group or message
ClaimPage.contact_referral: A friend or someone I know
ClaimPage.contact_search: A search result or a site I found
ClaimPage.amount_label: About how much did you lose?
ClaimPage.amount_hint: For example 2,500 USDT. We work out the real figure from the chain.
ClaimPage.others_unnamed: {count, plural, =0 {No one else has reported a matching payment yet.} one {1 other person has reported something that matches.} other {# other people have reported something that matches.}}
ClaimPage.hint_investment_platform: What returns were you promised, and by whom? How did you hear about it? What did you pay, and when? When did withdrawals stop, and were you asked for a fee or tax to release your money?
ClaimPage.hint_rug_pull: What was the project, and who promoted it and where? What did you buy and when? What happened to the token and to the team afterwards?
ClaimPage.hint_exchange_service: What service was it and what did you hold there? When did withdrawals stop? What were you told, and what have you tried since?
ClaimPage.hint_impersonation: Who did they say they were, and how did they contact you? What did they ask you to do, and when did you realise? Did they use the same story with others you know of?
ClaimPage.hint_recovery_scam: Who offered to recover your money and how did they find you? What did you pay them, and what did they do or say afterwards? What was the loss they promised to recover?
ClaimPage.hint_wallet_drained: How do you think it happened (a link, an app, a message)? When did you notice? What did you do just before it? Which tokens left, and where did they go?
ClaimPage.hint_address_poisoning: Which address did you mean to pay, and which one did the money go to? Where did you copy it from? When did you notice, and how much was sent?
ClaimPage.hint_honeypot_token: What token was it, and where did you buy it? When did you find you could not sell? Was a fee charged on selling, and who promoted it?
ClaimPage.hint_extortion: How did they contact you, and what did they threaten? What did they ask for, and how much did you send? Have they asked again?
ClaimPage.hint_fake_job: How was the job or task offered? What were you asked to pay or deposit, and what were you promised? When did payments stop?
ClaimPage.hint_account_takeover: Which account was it, and when did you lose access? Did you lose phone service or get odd messages first? What left the account, and where did it go?
ClaimPage.hint_other: What happened, who was involved, what you paid and when, and what has happened since.
ClaimPage.own_lead: Add as many as you like. Never share your seed phrase.
ClaimPage.own_wallet_text: Your wallet will open and ask you to sign the message below. Check that the account is the one on your claim, then approve. It costs nothing.
ClaimPage.own_wallet_none: We can’t see a wallet in this browser. Open this page in your wallet’s browser, or sign by hand.
ClaimPage.own_wallet_wrong_wallet: Your wallet is connected with a different account. Switch to {address} and try again.
ClaimPage.own_wallet_rejected: You declined in your wallet, so nothing was signed.
ClaimPage.own_wallet_failed: Your wallet could not sign. You can sign by hand instead.
ClaimPage.own_wallet_signature: That signature does not match this wallet and message.
ClaimPage.own_hand_copy_text: This is exactly what you will sign. It names your wallet and has a one-time code, so it can’t be reused for another claim.
ClaimPage.own_hand_sign_title: Sign it and paste the signature
ClaimPage.own_hand_sign_text: In your wallet, sign the message as plain text, not as a transaction. Then paste the signature here.
ClaimPage.own_tool_etherscan: One tool signs on every Ethereum-style chain, so Etherscan works for this wallet.
ClaimPage.own_tool_tronscan: On Tronscan, open More, then Tools, then Sign & Verify.
ClaimPage.own_tool_none: There is no signing site for this chain. Use the sign-message feature in your wallet app.
ClaimPage.own_docs_text: Send anything that shows this wallet is yours. A person at Celia reads it and confirms the wallet.
ClaimPage.own_docs_example_app: A screenshot of your wallet app showing this address
ClaimPage.own_docs_example_receipt: A receipt or statement from the exchange or app the money was sent from
ClaimPage.own_docs_example_history: Your wallet’s transaction history for this address, as a screenshot or PDF
ClaimPage.own_docs_safe: Cover anything private. Never include a seed phrase or private key.
ClaimPage.own_docs_files_label: Files: PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF, up to {size} MB each, {count} at a time
ClaimPage.own_err_files_type: Only PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF files.
ClaimPage.own_err_files_size: Each file must be 4 MB or smaller.
ClaimPage.own_err_files_count: No more than 3 files at a time, and 6 for a claim.
ClaimPage.own_declined: We could not confirm the wallet yet: {note}
ClaimPage.own_video_text: Make a short video, put it online and drop the link here. We review it for what it shows about your case and your wallet. Two to five minutes is plenty.
ClaimPage.own_video_show_who: Say your name, today’s date and the name of the platform.
ClaimPage.own_video_show_wallet: Show your wallet app with this address on screen.
ClaimPage.own_video_show_tx: Open the transaction where your money left and show that it matches your claim.
ClaimPage.own_video_show_sign: If you can, sign the message from the last step, or send a tiny transaction, while recording.
ClaimPage.own_video_show_story: Explain what you were promised, what you paid and what happened.
ClaimPage.own_video_safe: Never show or read out your seed phrase or private key. Cover any balances or details you want to keep private.
ClaimPage.own_video_where: Record with your phone or computer, then upload it to Loom, YouTube (set to unlisted) or Google Drive and copy the share link. Anyone with the link must be able to watch it.
ClaimPage.own_video_loom_help: New to Loom? <link>See how to record a video and copy its link.</link>
ClaimPage.own_video_link_error: Enter a link that starts with https://
ClaimPage.own_video_quality: We strongly recommend the best quality you can manage: record at the highest resolution, keep the wallet address and the transaction readable on screen, and speak clearly with good light and sound. A clear video is much easier to rely on.
ClaimPage.own_tool_bitcoin: Wallets such as Sparrow, Electrum, Ledger Live and Trezor Suite can sign a message. Use a regular address, not a Taproot one (starting bc1p).
ClaimPage.own_sec_sign_text: Shows you hold the wallet now. Checked straight away.
ClaimPage.own_sign_unsupported: We can’t check signatures on this chain yet.
ClaimPage.own_sec_video_text: Record your screen and drop the link.
ClaimPage.own_withdraw_hint: Deletes your files and the link. A video stays where you uploaded it, so delete it there too.
ClaimPage.own_record_hint: A dated page of what you added, with a fingerprint of each file. Print it or share it.
ClaimPage.followup_text: We keep these details only so Celia can follow up on your claim. They are not shared with anyone, including lawyers, firms and organisations, unless you explicitly agree. You can change or delete them at any time.
ClaimPage.followup_channel_email: Email, the address on my account
ClaimPage.followup_saved: Saved. Only Celia can see this.
ClaimPage.followup_error_value: Add a number or handle so we can reach you.
